newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end nearly flat, overall mood weak.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end nearly flat, overall mood weak.

text.p: Stocks closed little changed on Monday but declining stocks well outpaced advancers as the overall sentiment remained gloomy, brokers said.
They said the investors' sentiment was depressed by the huge amount of margin loans investors owed to brokerage houses which must be paid back this month.
The composite index closed 0.15 points higher at a provisional 781.88, after ranging from 780.88 to 788.40.
"There is no incentive for investors to buy shares. Gains by a handful of heavyweight stocks kept the index higher," said an LG Securities broker. Decliners beat advancers by 521 to 310.
Brokers said blue chips, heavily weighted on the composite index, rose on bargain hunting and some foreign buying.
Samsung Electronics rose 1,600 won to 58,500 and Pohang Iron and Steel added 200 won to 46,700. Korea Electric Power Corp ended 200 won up to 26,800.

"The blue-chip strength is mainly based on bargain hunting that will be short-lived," said a Hyundai Securities broker. "The overall market prospects still look gloomy with little chance of immediate recovery."
Margin loans that investors must pay back over the next two months are estimated at about 200 billion won, brokers said.
"As customer deposits remain at a relatively low level, selling is expected to increase to pay back the loans," said a Dongwon Securities broker.
Customer deposits at brokerages are currently at 2.3 trillion won.
The index futures December contracts ended 0.45 points lower at 81.85, while the KOSPI 200 index rose 0.03 points to 82.23.
